POSITION OVERVIEW

We at PEOPLE CAST PTY LTD are seeking a skilled General Butcher to work on a full-time basis at a meat processing facility located in Wangara, Western Australia.

A competitive salary and a genuine long-term career opportunity is available for the right candidates.

POSITION SKILLS REQUIREMENTS

We are seeking a candidate who possess the skills to select, cut, trim, prepare and arrange meat for sale and supply, operate meat and smallgoods processing machines, and manage the processes involved in the production of smallgoods as required.

POSITION QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE, AND ABILITIES REQUIREMENTS

We are seeking a candidate who possess the following qualifications, experience, and abilities:

1. Relevant AQF Certificate III Qualification, including at least two years of on-the-job training, or relevant AQF Certificate IV Qualification preferred.

2. 1-3 years of relevant, full-time employment experience preferred.

3. Ability to work on a full-time basis.

POSITION SALARY

$79,632.80 per annum (+ super).

POSITION APPLICATIONS

Please send an up-to-date resume, together with a covering letter addressing how you meet the criteria for skills, qualifications, experience, and abilities that the position demands, by email to dcarey@agnewirm.com.au, with the Workforce Australia Job ID included in your email subject line.

No telephone calls at this stage please.

With the recent installation and commissioning of three state-of-the-art IGM Robotic Welding Systems at Bowhill Engineering, we are growing our Robotics Team & seek an additional Robotic Welder Operator


This is an exciting & unique
opportunity to work with world-class technology in our new B5 Fabrication Hall, contributing to the production of over 660 precision-engineered steel tunnel segments for the Torrens to Darlington
Project & future heavy structural steel projects.


Specialising in large government infrastructure projects and complexity done excellently, Bowhill
Engineering is powered by technology, driven by great people to optimize and build structures that matter.


About the Role
Advancing Bowhill Engineering’s robotic capabilities, a blend of technical skills, knowledge of welding processes, and familiarity with robotic programming and maintenance is key to success in this role.


Through the daily operating, maintaining, and programming you will ensure efficient, high-quality welds & products and look to increase cost effectiveness of manufacturing operations of our robotic welding systems. Proficiency with CAD software or similar tools, experience in quality control, and understanding of safety protocols are highly beneficial.


Sharing our big picture focus, on enhancing production efficiency, implementing improvements and increasing our robotic capabilities, you will play a key role in operating advanced robotic welding
cells, deliver high performance & specialized welding requirements to produce high-quality fabrication outcomes.


Key Responsibilities & Requirements
Ability to operate fully automated robotic welding systemsCapability to develop advanced offline and online welding programsStrong fault-finding and troubleshooting skillsStrong work ethic and commitment to quality


Robot Operator/Welder Experience & Qualification
Trade Certification (Welding or Fabrication) or relevant on-the-job welding experienceExperience reading and interpreting engineering drawingsHigh Risk Forklift Licence (highly desirable)


What We Offer
Cutting-edge robotic welding technologyWork Diversity - major infrastructure project of national significancePermanent position with long-term stabilityAnnual wage reviews and wage boost incentivesDay and Afternoon shifts available (Afternoon shift attracts a 15% loading on hourly rates)Relocation incentive or accommodation assistance *subject to conditionsEmployee Assistance Program (EAP)Employee Health AssistanceActive Social Club and strong team environmentCareer advancement opportunities within a growing organisationModern workplace with 5 workshops on siteEnjoy the River Murray lifestyleJoin the Employer of Choice in the Murraylands, with a great workplace culture and team

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Requisition Number: REQ674383
Employment Type: Temporary Part - Time 
Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Educator
Remuneration: $120,652.51- $124,565.90 per annum, pro rata (+ super + 17.5% leave loading where applicable) 
Hours per week: 20 Hours per week
Applications Close: 22 July 2026
Vaccination Category: A
Located in: Culcairn

Lead Learning. Inspire Excellence. Grow Nursing in Culcairn.
 

Culcairn offers the best of rural living, with affordable housing, a welcoming community and short commutes that create the perfect work-life balance. Enjoy local parks, Billabong Creek and sporting clubs, or take a short drive to Albury for shopping, dining and wineries, or Wagga Wagga for even more recreation and entertainment. Just 40 minutes from Albury-Wodonga and an hour from Wagga Wagga, Culcairn is the ideal place to build a rewarding career while enjoying a relaxed country lifestyle.

About the Opportunity-

As a Clinical Nurse Educator (CNE) at Culcairn Health Service, you will be instrumental in the development and career success of the nursing team. You will be the go-to expert for nursing education, providing engaging evidence-based programs and support to enhance clinical knowledge and skills. Reap the benefit of your patient and customised approach to education; ensuring all nursing staff can apply their learning to clinical practice and deliver safe, high-quality healthcare.

As the CNE, and ideal candidate you will:

Deliver and coordinate clinical education and professional development

Orientate, supervise and mentor staff, students and TPP participants

Promote clinical leadership, best practice and a positive learning culture

Contribute to district-wide education, training and policy development

Provide unit-based and individual education and skill support

Delegate and support Nurses and others within scope of practice

Maintain contemporary practice and meet CNE-CME Framework requirements

Participate in audits, quality activities and care delivery aligned with safety standards

To find out more, please review the Position Description

Why join MLHD?

At Murrumbidgee Local Health District (MLHD), we offer more than a job - we offer the chance to make a real difference.

Meaningful Impact - Play a vital role in supporting essential services to our diverse and vibrant regional communities.

Flexible Working Arrangements - Designed to support work-life balance, aligned with NSW Health policy.

Generous Salary Packaging - Access up to $20,600 per annum tax-free for living expenses, plus the option for novated car leasing.

Professional Development - Take advantage of ongoing learning and career development opportunities.

Health & Wellbeing Support - Benefit from our comprehensive wellness programs for you and your family, including Employee Assistance Programs Fitness Passport and initiatives to support both physical and mental health.

Click here to discover why MLHD is the right place to contribute to healthier communities.

How to Apply 
If this sounds like the opportunity for you, click apply now! Please contact Daryl Mitchell- Facility Manager, via email, Daryl.Mitchell@health.nsw.gov.au , if you have any questions about this role.

This is a NSW Health Category A position which requires immunisation and screening for certain diseases. The full list of requirements are outlined in the NSW Health OASV Policy (Page 11). You will be required to complete the OASV Undertaking- Declaration Form and TB Assessment Tool during the recruitment process. Please upload this with your application along with any other vaccination evidence that you may have.

MLHD welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and is committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve.
We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disability, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and the LGBTIQ+ community.

If you identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, you can access recruitment application support through the Stepping Up initiative.

With a proven end-to-end solution that includes design, draft, certification, fabrication and on-site installation, the highly qualified and experienced team at Key Solutions Group will work closely with you to deliver each project on time, on budget and to the high standard we are known for.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Understand surface preparation and finishes.
Be able to understand and complete works to specifications.
Be able to mix to correct ratio two-part paint coatings etc.
Select paints, varnishes and stains to various surfaces using brushes, sprays, and rollers.
Understand the use of Wet Film Thickness Gauges and be able to achieve specified dry film thickness.
Be able to work at heights and in confined spaces.
Erecting scaffolding and ladders.
Cleaning equipment and work areas.

Desirable traits and will highly be regarded:
Trade Certificate –Certificate III in Surface Preparation or equivalent (for Blaster/Painters)
Construction Induction (White or Blue Card)
High Risk Licence for EWP and/or Forklift
Trade Qualifications in Protective Coatings (ACA, NACE, ICorr, or other trade certs)
HR licence, high risk licence with EWP and Forklift
Drivers Licence (MR or HR class)

Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Strong communication skills
With tight attention to detail
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!

result.description: True Protein   About the role:   We’re looking for an experienced Production Operations Supervisor to oversee daily operations, train and manage a small team, and help bring our new automated facility at Braeside to life. This factory and role would be working under the True Protein’s group of companies.  You’ll be working in a clean, modern environment with a new CP6000 canning machine at its heart. If you’re the kind of person who thrives when given real ownership and wants to see the direct results of your work, you’ll fit right in.         Benefits   What’s In It for You:    Competitive salary package  A modern semi-automated production facility  Supportive and collaborative environment  Opportunity to work with an innovative Australian manufacturing business with career progression opportunities       Task & responsibilities   Oversee daily production operations and ensuring output targets are achieved  Manage and monitor all operating machinery, ensuring optimal performance and uptime  Supervise and coordinate the packing line, robotic and pallet wrapping systems to maintain efficiency and product quality  Conduct staff training and development activities (where capability permits) to build team skills and compliance  Provide hands-on operational cover during staff breaks and absences across all production areas  Ensure all workplace health and safety protocols are followed on the production floor  Communicate effectively with Management regarding production progress, staffing issues, and equipment status  Assist with quality control checks and production reporting as required  Manage rosters, leave, and recruitment    Qualification & experience   Qualifications in Engineering and or Supply Chain Management  12 months minimum work experience in a related field is required  Hands-on experience in food or beverage manufacturing management  Comfortable operating and maintaining automated processing and packaging machinery  A natural leader who builds capable, motivated teams  Familiarity with food safety standards (HACCP, GMP) and WHS legislation  Sharp problem-solver who reads the data and drives real improvements  Flexible — happy to step in and assist across all operational areas when needed  Current forklift licence (desirable)   About Company     About True:   At True, we're on a mission to create a world of healthier people.  True Protein was born out of a desire to empower our community in living energetic and fulfilled lives. Since 2014, we have pioneered a new standard in health and performance products, delivering natural, authentic and transparent products without compromise.   This all begins within our own True Team, a high performing group of like-minded individuals who truly believe in and strive to embody our company values in all that we do, both in our personal and professional lives. About the Role:  
We are seeking enthusiastic  Graduate Radiographers  to join our client’s welcoming and professional team in Rockhampton, QLD. Whether you're set to graduate in 2025/26 or have recently completed your degree, this is a unique opportunity to begin your career with a strong foundation in both public and private imaging settings. You’ll gain hands-on experience, training in CT, and work closely with on-site Radiologists and experienced imaging professionals. 

  Key Responsibilities:  

 Deliver general X-ray imaging with professionalism and care across multiple locations. 

 Begin structured CT training within your first few months of employment. 

 Rotate across hospital and private practice environments to build a versatile skill set. 

 Participate in shift work and on-call rosters (with additional earning opportunities). 

 Accurately record services and patient information using RIS/PACS systems. 

 Commit to continuous professional development and CPD-supported learning. 

 Contribute to a positive team culture and uphold patient safety and dignity at all times. 

  Skills and Qualifications:  

 Recent or upcoming graduate in Medical Imaging (Bachelor of Science or equivalent). 

 Eligible for AHPRA registration (2025/26 graduates encouraged to apply). 

 Queensland Radiation Use Licence (or eligibility to obtain). 

 Excellent communication and teamwork skills. 

 Keen interest in learning CT, with future options for MRI training. 

 Australian work rights or eligibility for visa sponsorship. 

  Benefits:  

 Competitive hourly rates plus shift and on-call allowances. 

 Full-time employment in a high-growth, coastal location just 1 hour from Brisbane. 

 Structured CT training provided early in your career. 

 Regular social and professional events to support a vibrant team culture. 

 CPD support, education allowances, and professional memberships paid annually. 

 Opportunities for career progression across multiple imaging modalities. 

 Affordable housing, great lifestyle by the coast, and supportive leadership. 

 Annual salary reviews to reward growing skills and experience. 

  More About Our Client:  
Our client is a leading provider of diagnostic imaging services, recognized for its commitment to quality, innovation, and patient care. With a strong presence across Regional/Coastal Australia, they operate a network of practices and partner with private facilities and public hospitals to deliver exceptional radiology services. 

  Ready to Apply?  
Submit your resume and cover letter to us now.      Apply Now

Join MEGT as an Electrical Apprentice! 
 Are you a motivated, reliable and hands-on individual looking to launch your career in the electrical industry? MEGT has a fantastic opportunity with one of our valued clients for an  Electrical Apprenticeship  based in  Port Macquarie, NSW , with work completed across surrounding areas.   
 About the role 
 This apprenticeship offers a unique opportunity to develop practical skills and gain hands-on experience in the  domestic electrical industry . You will work alongside experienced electricians while completing a nationally recognised qualification.   You will gain experience in:   
 
 Assisting qualified electricians with a variety of domestic electrical work. 
 Learning the fundamentals of electrical installations, maintenance and repairs. 
 Using and maintaining electrical tools and equipment under supervision. 
 Completing general site support duties while developing practical electrical skills. 
 
 What we're looking for 
 
 Punctual, reliable and motivated, with a strong work ethic and willingness to learn. 
 Strong mathematical ability, with a demonstrated commitment to achieving good results in mathematics. 
 A current White Card is essential. 
 A driver's licence and reliable transport are preferred. 
 Completion of an electrical pre-apprenticeship or relevant technical college course is desirable but not essential. 
 
 Previous experience using hand tools or power tools is not required. The successful candidate will receive training and support and should be willing to listen, follow instructions and learn from the ground up.   
 What can you expect from us? 
 
 Personalised one-on-one mentoring and support throughout your apprenticeship. 
 A nationally recognised qualification. 
 Weekly pay. 
 Comprehensive TAFE training leading to a  Certificate III in Electrotechnology (Electrician) . 
 Hands-on experience across a variety of domestic electrical projects. 
 
 What other benefits? 
 
 Work alongside experienced electricians who will provide practical guidance and support. 
 Gain exposure to a range of domestic electrical work across different job sites. 
 Opportunities to attend industry and social events hosted by electrical wholesalers and suppliers. 
 Build valuable industry connections and a strong foundation for a long-term career in the electrical industry. 
 Potential ongoing employment opportunities upon completion, subject to business requirements and performance. 
 
 About the company 
 Our client is a locally based electrical business operating from  Port Macquarie, NSW , specialising in  domestic electrical work  across surrounding areas. The team provides a supportive, hands-on learning environment where apprentices receive direct guidance and practical experience across a variety of residential projects.   The employer is open to candidates with no previous electrical experience and is committed to teaching the successful apprentice the skills required to build a successful career in the electrical industry. If you are motivated, willing to listen and eager to learn, this could be the opportunity for you.    Please note:  The role involves travelling to different residential job sites. The successful candidate will generally meet the team at the Wauchope workshop at approximately  6:30 am  before travelling to job locations in a company vehicle. Working hours may vary depending on project requirements.    Interested?  Click  "Apply Now"  or visit   https://www.megt.com.au/jobs   for more information.   At MEGT, we enable people to start their careers through Apprenticeships and Traineeships and support large and small businesses to recruit, train and grow careers. Our purpose is to provide life-changing, lifelong learning and employment solutions for all. We invite you to be part of our story. By applying, you agree to receive information about other MEGT employment and education opportunities.   MEGT is committed to being a Child Safe Organisation and an Equal Opportunity Employer. We have zero tolerance for racism, discrimination, harm or abuse. We have a culture that values safety, diversity and inclusion and encourage all qualified applicants, including women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, veterans and individuals from diverse backgrounds, to apply.
